resources.string: On a computer with a web browser, install rclone from rclone.org/downloads.
In a terminal on that computer run: rclone authorize \"%1$s\" — then sign in and allow access in the browser window that opens.
Copy the JSON text rclone prints between the arrows (starting with { and ending with }) and paste it into the Token field below.
After saving, set the destination folder to start with the bucket name, for example my-bucket/phone-backups.
Amazon S3
Store backups in an Amazon Web Services S3 bucket using an access key.
In the AWS console, create an IAM user limited to your backup bucket (s3:ListBucket, s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject, s3:DeleteObject).
Create an access key for that user and copy the access key ID and the secret access key.
MinIO (self-hosted S3)
Store backups on your own MinIO server or any S3-compatible storage you run.
In the MinIO console, create an access key for a user that may write to your backup bucket, and note the server\'s API address.
Wasabi
Store backups in Wasabi hot cloud storage through its S3 API.
In the Wasabi console, open Access Keys, create a new key and copy both parts. Use the service URL of your bucket\'s region as the endpoint.
Cloudflare R2
Store backups in Cloudflare R2 object storage, with no egress fees for restores.
In the Cloudflare dashboard, open R2 and choose Manage R2 API Tokens. Create a token with Object Read & Write permission.
Copy the access key ID, the secret access key and the S3 endpoint shown for your account.
Backblaze B2
Store backups in Backblaze B2 cloud storage using an application key.
In your Backblaze account, open Application Keys and add a new key, ideally restricted to your backup bucket.
Copy the keyID and the applicationKey right away; Backblaze shows the key only once.
Google Drive
Store backups in your Google Drive. Sign-in happens once on a computer.
Choose \"drive\" for full access, or \"drive.file\" so DFTB only sees the files it created.
Microsoft OneDrive
Store backups in OneDrive personal, OneDrive for Business or SharePoint.
OneDrive also needs a drive ID: on the computer, create the remote with rclone config, then run rclone config show and copy drive_id and drive_type.
Dropbox
Store backups in your Dropbox. Sign-in happens once on a computer.
MEGA
Store backups in your MEGA account with its end-to-end encrypted storage.
Enter the e-mail address and password of your MEGA account.
If two-factor sign-in is turned on for the account, MEGA may refuse the login; turn it off for this account or use a separate MEGA account for backups.
pCloud
Store backups in your pCloud storage. Sign-in happens once on a computer.
Pick eapi.pcloud.com if your account is in the EU region, otherwise keep api.pcloud.com.
Box
Store backups in Box. Sign-in happens once on a computer.
Box replaces its refresh token every time it is used. Once DFTB has used this remote, do not reuse the same token on the computer.
SFTP (through rclone)
Reach an SSH server through rclone, for example to share one remote definition with your desktop.
Enter the server address and your account name.
Sign in with a password, or paste a private key (PEM or OpenSSH format) together with its passphrase if it has one. One of the two is required.
Nextcloud (WebDAV)
Store backups on a Nextcloud server through WebDAV.
In Nextcloud, open Settings, then Security, and create an app password for DFTB.
Use the WebDAV address shown under Files settings, which looks like https://cloud.example.com/remote.php/dav/files/USERNAME/.
